samples.summary: prepareFenceSource() runs its fetch-refusal checks on the RAW source but hands the engine the POST-strip text, so a `%%{…}%%` directive spliced into a forbidden construct bypasses every refusal
samples.evidence: In `prepareFenceSource()` (mermaid.ts:384-403) `FETCH_TAG_RE`, `IMAGE_METADATA_RE` and `hasCssFetch()` are tested against `source`, and only afterwards is `stripConfigDirectives(source)` computed and returned as `prepared.text` — which is what `mermaid.render()` receives at line 672. The strip JOINS the text around each removed directive; the module's own doc comment already states this (line 298-299: "Directive removal can promote a directive too, by joining text around the match"), but the fetch checks never re-run on the joined result. Concrete exploit, entirely inside the primary diagram type: ```mermaid flowchart LR A@%%{x}%%{ img: "https://attacker.example/beacon.png" } ``` Raw source: `IMAGE_METADATA_RE` (`/@\s*\{[\s\S]*?["']?img["']?\s*:/i`, line 351) does not match because the character after `@` is `%`, not `{`/whitespace. `FETCH_TAG_RE` and `hasCssFetch()` do not match either. `DIRECTIVE_RE` then deletes `%%{x}%%` (it matches `%%{` + `\s*` + `(\w+)`=`x` + empty optional group + `}%%`), leaving `A@{ img: "https://attacker.example/beacon.png" }` — exactly the source the new check exists to refuse — which is passed to `mermaid.render()`. Per the change's own analysis (lines 74-78) that reaches `imageSquare()`, which does `new Image(); img.src = node.img; await img.decode()` and appends an SVG `` to the live `d` layout host: two requests from every reader's browser, upstream of `sanitizeSvg()`, disclosing IP/User-Agent/reading time to the note author. The same splice defeats the other two checks: `A->>B: ` becomes `` after the strip (the unguarded-`foreignObject` label paths described at lines 79-83 then lay it out), and `style A background:u%%{x}%%rl("https://attacker.example/b.png")` becomes a live `url(` in a style declaration. Fix: run the refusal checks on the stripped text (or on both raw and stripped), i.e. strip first, then scan.

samples.summary: FETCH_TAG_RE is a tag-name denylist and misses the `background` attribute carriers (`<table>`/`<td>`/`<tr>`/`<body>`…), which mermaid's own default-allowlist sanitizer keeps and the browser resolves to a background-image fetch during layout
samples.evidence: `FETCH_TAG_RE` (line 338-339) enumerates fetch-capable TAGS only. The HTML `background` attribute on `body`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `td`, `th` is mapped to `background-image` by the HTML rendering spec and implemented by Chrome/Firefox, and DOMPurify's default HTML attribute allowlist (what mermaid's strict-mode `sanitizeText()` uses, per the change's own note at lines 79-83) includes `background`. So a label on one of the diagram types that emits a `foreignObject` regardless of `htmlLabels` — e.g. `sequenceDiagram\n A->>B: x` — survives mermaid's sanitizer, is parsed into the live layout host in `document.body`, and fetches the URL before `sanitizeSvg()` runs. `hasCssFetch()` does not see it (the value is a bare URL, no `url(`/`@import`), and `FORBID_ATTR: ['ping','srcset','background',…]` at line 430 only governs what PERSISTS, which the module explicitly says is not a fetch boundary (line 52-53). I could not install node_modules on this branch to confirm the exact DOMPurify default attr list and the exact set of mermaid label paths, hence medium confidence; the vector is the same class the change is closing.

samples.summary: SECURE_KEYS pins only the `flowchart` and `class` config sections by hand; any other section carrying a fetch- or label-relevant key is unpinned, and nothing asserts the list against the engine's schema
samples.evidence: `SECURE_KEYS` (lines 208-237) is a hand-maintained list, and the two per-diagram sections added are chosen from a read of the pinned 11.16.0 build. `secure` pins TOP-LEVEL keys only (stated at line 233), so any other diagram section that carries `htmlLabels`, a `dompurifyConfig`, or theming (e.g. `state`, `sequence`, `mindmap`, `er`, `architecture`) would still accept a nested override from a directive that layer 2's strip under-recognizes — which is precisely the residual-risk model the file documents for the strip. Nothing in the suite compares this list against the installed engine's config schema the way `MERMAID_CARRIER_PATTERNS_VERSION` pins the carrier regexes, so a minor upgrade that adds `htmlLabels` to another section is silent. Defense-in-depth only, since layer 2 normally removes the carrier.

samples.summary: MAX_FENCE_CHARS bounds one fence, not one note, so the stored-work bound the strip cap advertises is per-fence and multiplies by the number of fences a note carries
samples.evidence: `prepareFenceSource()` caps `source.length` per placeholder (line 385) and `stripConfigDirectives()` caps passes at 8, so the doc's bound (`MAX_FENCE_CHARS * MAX_STRIP_PASSES`) holds per fence. `collectPending()` (line 548) collects every `.note-mermaid` placeholder in the note with no cap, and `renderPass()` scans/strips each one on every keystroke, so a note with N hostile fences costs N × 400 kB of regex scanning per re-render, and each near-bound fence still pays 8 full passes before being refused. Lower impact than the guard bypasses above and partly the correctness/perf lane's concern, but it is the same stored-main-thread-cost argument the change makes for the pass bound.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the finding describes. FETCH_TAG_RE (mermaid.ts:338-339) is a tag-name-only denylist containing no `background`-attribute carriers (`table`, `tbody`/`thead`/`tfoot`, `tr`, `td`, `th`, `body`), and prepareFenceSource (mermaid.ts:384-404) contains no other check that would catch such a tag: IMAGE_METADATA_RE (351) matches only `@{ img: }` shape metadata, and CSS_SOURCE_FETCH_RE (364-365) requires `@import`/`image-set(`/`cross-fade(`/`url(`, so a bare URL in `background="https://…"` is invisible to hasCssFetch(). I grepped all of packages/notes for any other source-level guard on raw HTML or `background`: none exists. Reachability is asserted by the module's own load-bearing design notes — lines 51-53 state mermaid lays the diagram out in a host div in document.body BEFORE sanitizeSvg() runs and that layer 3 "is not a fetch boundary", and lines 79-83 state that venn/architecture/kanban/sequence append a foreignObject with no htmlLabels guard whose contents pass only mermaid's strict-mode DOMPurify default allowlist; PURIFY_CONFIG re-adds `foreignobject` (421) because those subtrees really appear. The only place `background` is blocked is FORBID_ATTR at line 430, which is in sanitizeSvg() — strictly downstream of the layout fetch by the file's own account — so it governs persistence, not the request. That makes this an added-but-bypassable gate: `<table background="https://attacker.example/beacon.png">` (or `<table><td background=…>`) in a label on one of those diagram types reaches the live layout host and fetches, disclosing every reader's IP/User-Agent/reading time to the note author — the exact threat class the change exists to close. Refutation grounds all fail: not-present (code matches), already-guarded (only guard is downstream of the fetch), out-of-scope (untrusted-collaborator-driven sensitive data exposure is in the security lane). The reviewer's literal `<td …>` standalone payload would likely be dropped by HTML fragment parsing, but the `<table background=…>` form is unaffected, so the class holds; I also could not install node_modules (no dompurify/mermaid in tree) to pin DOMPurify's default attribute list, which is a reason to keep the finding rather than drop it.

finding.summary: `htmlLabels: false` does not close the layout-window beacon class: mermaid's shape metadata (`A@{ img: "https://attacker/beacon" }`, icon shapes) emits an SVG `<image href>` into the live layout host regardless of label mode
finding.evidence: The fix's whole claim (module note lines 51-63, docs `notes.md`) is that with `htmlLabels: false` "there is no label subtree to lay out", so nothing fetches during measurement. Mermaid 11 node metadata carries an image shape independent of label rendering — `flowchart LR\n  A@{ img: "https://attacker.example/beacon.png" }` — which the renderer materializes as an SVG `<image href=…>` inside the `d<id>` host div appended to `document.body` (mermaid.ts:518-520 documents that host). The browser fetches that href the moment it is parsed, i.e. strictly before `sanitizeSvg()` runs, so the note author still gets every reader's IP, UA and read time. `FORBID_TAGS: ['img','image', …]` (mermaid.ts:281) removes it only from what persists — the exact reasoning error the change's own lessons doc identifies. Same shape of residual carrier for `icon:` shapes if an icon pack is ever registered. I could not confirm against the installed engine (no `node_modules/mermaid` in the tree, so I could not grep `imageSquare`/shape handling), hence medium confidence; nothing in the diff or the suite tests a non-label fetch carrier.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `htmlLabels: false` is the whole defense and that mermaid's `@{ img: … }` shape-metadata carrier reaches the live layout host unguarded, with only downstream `FORBID_TAGS` to clean it up. The repository already guards exactly that carrier upstream of the layout window. `IMAGE_METADATA_RE` (mermaid.ts:351) matches `@{ … img: }` shape metadata, and `prepareFenceSource()` (mermaid.ts:393-395) returns 'Diagram error: image shapes are not allowed' for it; `renderPass()` (mermaid.ts:663-668) short-circuits on that error so `mermaid.render()` (mermaid.ts:672, the only production render call site in the repo) is never invoked — no `d` host is created, no `new Image().decode()`, no SVG `` parsed, hence no request. The module note the finding quotes says the opposite of what is attributed to it: mermaid.ts:70-83 explicitly states "`htmlLabels: false` alone does NOT close that window" and names `imageSquare()` and the unguarded `foreignObject` diagram types as the reasons the source-level refusals exist. The companion raw-HTML carrier is covered by FETCH_TAG_RE (mermaid.ts:339, checked at 390) and CSS fetches by hasCssFetch (mermaid.ts:396). The claim that neither diff nor suite tests a non-label fetch carrier is also false: preview.test.ts:750-773 uses the finding's exact payload and asserts `engine.render` was not called, and preview.test.ts:775-792 covers the raw-`` sequence-label path. The residual `icon:` variant is conditioned on a registered icon pack, and a repo-wide grep finds no `registerIconPacks`/`iconPacks` call anywhere in source, so no such path is reachable today.

Not every label path goes through that chain: mermaid reads `evaluate(getConfig().flowchart.htmlLabels)` directly in its edge-label/legacy label helpers, and `flowchart.htmlLabels` defaults to true — so `A -- "" --> B` (edge label rather than node label) would still be measured as a `` HTML subtree in the live document, refiring the exact issue #721 beacon. Mermaid's own strict-mode `sanitizeText` uses DOMPurify's DEFAULT allowlist (it only adds `FORBID_TAGS: ['style']`), which permits `` — which is why the original bug existed at all. The change also documents (PURIFY_CONFIG comment mermaid.ts:259-264, notes.md, lessons doc) that venn text nodes, architecture icons, kanban and sequence emit `foreignObject` "with no `htmlLabels` guard"; note text reaching those subtrees is the same pre-fetch window, and the lessons doc justifies leaving them with "`img`/`image` are already forbidden" — i.e. layer 3, which the same document correctly says is not a fetch boundary. verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — "Only the ROOT `htmlLabels` is set" — is not present in the code. `mermaid.initialize()` at packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:631-640 sets `htmlLabels: false`, `flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }` AND `class: { htmlLabels: false }`, i.e. the per-diagram key the reviewer says defaults to true is explicitly pinned false. `SECURE_KEYS` additionally pins the `flowchart` and `class` sections whole (mermaid.ts:235-236), with the in-code rationale (mermaid.ts:230-234) matching the reviewer's own argument that `secure` only pins top-level keys. The comment at mermaid.ts:619-630 does not stop at the root-first resolver — it names `swimlane`'s `evaluate(siteConfig.flowchart.htmlLabels)` and a shape's `getConfig().flowchart?.htmlLabels` as the exact reason both altitudes are set. The reviewer's proposed hardening ("also pin flowchart/class: { htmlLabels: false }") is literally the shipped code; tests assert it at preview.test.ts:632-648 and :663-666. Secondarily, the stated exploit is unreachable anyway: the claimed edge-label payload and the venn/architecture/kanban/sequence unguarded-`foreignObject` paths are refused before the engine ever runs, because `prepareFenceSource()` tests `FETCH_TAG_RE` (mermaid.ts:338-339, matches ``) and asserts `engine.render` is not called. finding.summary: The new fixpoint loop makes carrier stripping quadratic in an unbounded, attacker-controlled fence body — a stored main-thread DoS on every reader; the `maxTextSize` bound the comment leans on is enforced only inside `mermaid.render()`, i.e. after the strip
finding.evidence:
`stripConfigDirectives()` now loops (mermaid.ts:251-255). Each iteration removes at most ONE front-matter block (`FRONTMATTER_RE` is non-global and `^`-anchored) but pays a full global `DIRECTIVE_RE` scan plus two whole-string allocations, so a fence of k stacked `---
x
---
` blocks costs O(k·N) ≈ O(N²/8). The comment's own numbers confirm the scaling: 1.5 ms at 10 kB, 29 ms at 50 kB (≈20x for 5x input). It is called at mermaid.ts:504 on the raw fence body — mermaid's `maxTextSize` guard runs inside `mermaid.render()`, after the strip, so the 50 kB figure is not a bound on this input. I found no note/fence length cap anywhere in packages/notes (grepped for `maxTextSize`, `MAX_`, `slice(0,`, `content.length`) and `preview.ts:198` renders whatever the note contains. A collaborator or editor-role share-link visitor stores one ~2-5 MB fence of stacked front-matter blocks and every reader's tab freezes for minutes on open (the pass is synchronous on the main thread); several such fences in one note add up, and each theme switch re-keys the cache and re-pays it. Mitigation: cap the input length (or the iteration count) before looping, or make the front-matter pattern remove all leading blocks in one anchored pass.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — an unbounded fixpoint loop over an uncapped, attacker-controlled fence body — is not the code in this repository. (1) The loop is bounded, not a fixpoint: MAX_STRIP_PASSES = 8 (mermaid.ts:278) with `for (let pass = 0; pass < MAX_STRIP_PASSES; pass++)` (mermaid.ts:319) and a `return null` refusal when it has not converged (mermaid.ts:324). (2) The length cap the finding says is absent ("I found no note/fence length cap anywhere in packages/notes") exists and runs BEFORE the strip in the very same function: `if (source.length > MAX_FENCE_CHARS)` returns an error at mermaid.ts:385-389, and `stripConfigDirectives(source)` is only reached at mermaid.ts:399 after that early return; MAX_FENCE_CHARS = 50_000 at mermaid.ts:272. (3) The cited call site mermaid.ts:504 is wrong — that line is inside `sanitizeSvg()`; a repo-wide grep for `stripConfigDirectives`/`prepareFenceSource` finds the only production call sites at mermaid.ts:399 and mermaid.ts:663, so no path reaches the strip without the length cap. The claimed exploit (a ~2-5 MB stacked-front-matter fence) is refused at mermaid.ts:385 before the loop ever runs; residual worst-case work is MAX_FENCE_CHARS * MAX_STRIP_PASSES (~400 kB of scanning per fence), which is the bound the code's own comment at mermaid.ts:302-309 documents, including the very point about `maxTextSize` being enforced only inside `render()` (mermaid.ts:266-271). Both mitigations the finding proposes (cap the input length, cap the iteration count) are already implemented.

finding.summary: `SECURE_KEYS` — the layer-1 pin the change now relies on for `htmlLabels` — omits `dompurifyConfig`, the one config key that relaxes mermaid's own label sanitizer, turning a missed carrier from a beacon into script execution
finding.evidence: SECURE_KEYS (mermaid.ts:178-195) replaces mermaid's default `secure` list and enumerates theming/label keys, but not `dompurifyConfig`. Mermaid's strict-mode `sanitizeText` passes `config.dompurifyConfig` straight to DOMPurify, so a config carrier that layer 2 misses could deliver `{"dompurifyConfig":{"ADD_TAGS":["script"],"ADD_ATTR":["onerror"]}}` and get script/event-handler markup into any surviving HTML label subtree — which the engine parses into `document.body` during measurement (mermaid.ts:45-49), i.e. it executes before `sanitizeSvg()` exists. `legacyMathML`/`forceLegacyMathML` are similarly unpinned and switch KaTeX label output from MathML to HTML. The module's own stated model (mermaid.ts:32-35, notes.md 'a carrier the strip under-recognizes still delivers a nested override') is that layer 1's pin must hold when layer 2 misses, so this is a real gap in the defense the change strengthens. Related: `secure` pins top-level keys only, so the nested `flowchart.htmlLabels` the previous finding relies on cannot be pinned here at all — the diff's claim that the key is 'pinned in SECURE_KEYS … so a note cannot turn it back on' holds only for the root spelling.

verdict.reason: The finding's core absence claim is factually false in this working tree. SECURE_KEYS does contain 'dompurifyConfig' (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:229), preceded by a comment describing the exact attack the reviewer posits (mermaid.ts:225-228), and that array is the value passed as `secure:` to mermaid.initialize() on the live path (mermaid.ts:634), so the pin is enforced rather than decorative. A regression test asserts it (packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:663) and the design doc records it (docs/design/notes/notes.md:467). SECURE_KEYS is defined exactly once repo-wide (the only other `secure:` matches are unrelated backend cookie flags in packages/backend/src/auth/*). The reviewer's cited range mermaid.ts:178-195 does not correspond to SECURE_KEYS, which starts at line 208 — the quoted evidence describes a stale revision. The secondary claim that nested flowchart.htmlLabels "cannot be pinned here at all" is likewise refuted: 'flowchart' and 'class' are pinned as whole sections (mermaid.ts:235-236, asserted at preview.test.ts:665-666) and both are set to htmlLabels:false at initialize (mermaid.ts:637-638). The only residue is the passing mention of legacyMathML/forceLegacyMathML, which is not the finding's stated defect and carries no traced vector: <math> is refused at source by FETCH_TAG_RE (mermaid.ts:339) and any KaTeX output is still allowlist-sanitized by sanitizeSvg (mermaid.ts:499-521), so it does not sustain the major severity on its own.
